steps.title: to be · present
steps.html:
PersonPositiveNegativeQuestion
II am / I'm Turkish.I'm not Turkish.Am I late?
He / She / ItShe is / She's French.She isn't French.Is she French?
You / We / TheyThey are / They're British.They aren't British.Are they British?

In speech people almost always use the short form: I'm, she's, they're.

For a question, put am / is / are before the person.

Short answers: Yes, she is. / No, she isn't.

The past of these is was and were, from Lesson 1.

steps.title: One person, three countries
steps.html:
Rita Ora is a singer. She was born in Kosovo, but her family moved to London when she was a baby. She is British now, and she speaks English and Albanian. Her home town is London.

Sadio Mané is from Senegal. He is Senegalese, and French and Wolof are the languages of his country. He was a football player in England and in Germany, so he speaks English too. He isn't a Londoner, but he knows the city well.

Freddie Mercury was a singer from the band Queen. He wasn't British at the start of his life: he was born in Zanzibar, and his parents were from India. He came to England when he was seventeen. Today his name is famous in a hundred countries.
